WASHINGTON — U.S. job growth accelerated sharply in August while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, suggesting an improvement in the labor market after recent struggles, keeping an interest-rate increase from the Federal Reserve this month on the table.

The larger-than-expected increase in nonfarm payrolls last month reported by the Labor Department in its closely watched report Friday reflected a rebound in leisure and hospitality employment after two straight monthly declines, as well as a reversal of the drag from local government education.

Employers added just 57,000 jobs last month — less than half what economists expected — but the unemployment rate still fell to 4.2%. Workers kept quitting their jobs at an elevated clip of 3.07 million in May, signaling confidence they can find something better. And yet the share of working-age Americans actually in the labor force dropped to 61.5%, down from 61.8% the month before. # May 2026 jobs report: Employers add 172,000 jobs 

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that U.S. employers expanded payrolls by 172,000 jobs in May. That figure is well above economists’ projections of between 80,000 and 122,000 jobs. It marks the first time since early 2024 that the economy has seen 3 consecutive months of employment gains exceeding 100,000.

The May jobs report also notes that the U.S. economy saw 93,000 more jobs added than previously reported for March and April combined. March’s revised figure of 214,000 is the first monthly gain above 200,000 since early 2024, according to BLS data.

 Tayyub Yaqoob · 13 July 2026 · 4 min read 

Photograph: Bernd 📷 Dittrich / Unsplash

## Key takeaways

- Nonfarm payrolls rose 178,000 in March 2026; BLS said the unemployment rate "changed little at 4.3 percent", down from 4.4%.
- The civilian labour force shrank by 396,000 in March, from 170,483,000 to 170,087,000 — and household employment fell 64,000.
- The participation rate fell to 61.9% and the employment-population ratio to 59.2% — both lower than February.
- Average hourly earnings rose 0.2% on the month and 3.5% over the year, the smallest annual increase since May 2021.
- Between January and June 2026 — all months on the same population controls — the labour force fell by 1,107,000.
